rv.q: I can't fault her vocal performance here but there's no escaping that the storyline piles one cliché on another.
But in Memon’s liquid-gold singing voice, the emotional beats almost pierce your skin.
It's Memon's performance, oozing warmth and charisma, that makes this exceptionally crafted piece of gig theatre soar.
Manic Street Creature is a calling card for Memon’s considerable array of talents.
This is a hugely engaging and important piece of insightful theatre
This thought-provoking piece of gig theatre is exactly what London needs right now, and just to hear Memon’s magnificent voice is worth every penny – she is one to watch!
While Manic Street Creature doesn't always work as a piece of theatre, it absolutely does as a compelling, emotionally resonant showcase.

The material possesses moments of gentle comedy and touching pathos, most of all it has an inherent humanity and subtly asks us to consider the stark realities of mental health issues from different angles and perspectives.
The songs are wonderful and tell the story so clearly; it just felt like a few more songs instead of the spoken word towards the end could have really rocked the piece.
